newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kopper - no big German private bank mergers soon.
newsitem.headline: Kopper - no big German private bank mergers soon.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG's outgoing chief executive Hilmar Kopper said on Tuesday he did not expect large scale merger activity to break out among private sector German banks for a long time to come.

Kopper told the bank's annual shareholder meeting that he expected the domestic banking scene would undergo consolidation because it was "overbanked and overbranched," but he added that the mergers were initially most likely to occur among public sector and cooperative banks.
Kopper said media speculation of mergers and takeovers among private sector banks had been overblown.
Referring to the private sector, Kopper said: "apart from small cases I thing things will remain as they are for a long time to come."
Deutsche fuelled merger speculation by announcing last July it had acquired a 5.21 percent stake in Munich-based rival Bayerische Vereinsbank AG.
The bank said at the time it had no immediate plans to increase the stake and that the purchase was aimed at deterring potential rival bidders.
Kopper steps down at the end of the shareholder meeting and will become chairman of Deutsche's non-executive supervisory board.
He will be succeeded by Rolf Breuer, who has been on the management board since 1985.
